blogArticles.title: The Story Behind 100 Pieces
blogArticles.author: Percent Journal
blogArticles.excerpt: Why limitation creates freedom — and why every Percent design disappears after the hundredth piece.
blogArticles.introduction: A clear ending gives every design meaning. One hundred pieces is enough to create a community without making the experience ordinary.

image.alt: Limited Percent streetwear photographed in the city

secondaryImage.alt: Close view of premium apparel texture and construction

sections.heading: Why 100?
paragraphs: A fixed edition asks us to make clearer decisions. Every line, proportion and print has to earn its place before production begins.
The number is intentionally human: small enough to remain rare, yet large enough for one design to become part of many individual stories.

sections.heading: Why Not Restock?
paragraphs: Restocking would turn a promise into a marketing phrase. When the final piece leaves, the design is retired and the next idea gets room to exist.

sections.heading: Designing With an Ending
paragraphs: Knowing a design has an ending changes how we make it and how it is worn. The piece becomes a timestamp rather than an endlessly repeated product.

blogArticles.pullQuote: Once the hundredth piece is gone, that design becomes part of Percent history.

blogArticles.title: The Power of Limited
blogArticles.author: Percent Journal
blogArticles.excerpt: Why fewer pieces create stronger connections.
blogArticles.introduction: Limited design is not about creating urgency. It is about creating focus, value and a stronger relationship with what we choose to own.

image.alt: A considered streetwear collection in neutral tones

sections.heading: Fewer, Better Choices
paragraphs: When options become endless, character can disappear. A smaller edition gives one idea the space to be understood and remembered.

sections.heading: A Shared Connection
paragraphs: Every owner is part of a group that can never grow beyond the edition. The connection is quiet, but it is real.

sections.heading: Rarity With Purpose
paragraphs: For Percent, rarity is a result of restraint. We stop because the boundary is part of the design.

blogArticles.pullQuote: Limitation is not less possibility. It is more intention.

blogArticles.title: Intentional Design
blogArticles.author: Percent Journal
blogArticles.excerpt: A look into how Percent pieces move from idea to finished form.
blogArticles.introduction: Every Percent piece begins with a reason. The process removes what is unnecessary until the idea feels direct, wearable and distinct.

image.alt: Apparel materials used during the Percent design process

sections.heading: Start With Meaning
paragraphs: We begin with a thought rather than a trend. References are collected, challenged and reduced into one clear visual direction.

sections.heading: Refine the Form
paragraphs: Placement, scale and negative space are tested on the garment itself. The design has to work while moving, not only on a screen.

sections.heading: Finish With Restraint
paragraphs: A piece is ready when nothing feels accidental. Production begins only after the material and artwork support the same intention.

blogArticles.pullQuote: The strongest detail is often the one that knows when to stop.

blogArticles.title: Style in Real Life
blogArticles.author: Percent Journal
blogArticles.excerpt: How people make Percent their own.
blogArticles.introduction: A garment is unfinished until someone wears it. Personal styling gives every limited piece a second creative life beyond the studio.

image.alt: Streetwear styled with a personal point of view

sections.heading: One Piece, Different Stories
paragraphs: The same shirt can feel quiet, graphic, polished or relaxed depending on the person wearing it. That variation is the point.

sections.heading: Beyond the Lookbook
paragraphs: Campaign images introduce a direction. The community takes it further by mixing Percent with the clothes and objects that already matter to them.

sections.heading: Wear It Your Way
paragraphs: There is no required uniform. The most convincing style always looks lived in rather than prescribed.

blogArticles.pullQuote: Identity begins where styling rules end.

blogArticles.title: Inside the Studio
blogArticles.author: Percent Journal
blogArticles.excerpt: Ideas, experiments and everything between concept and production.
blogArticles.introduction: The studio is where unfinished thoughts become physical decisions through testing, comparison and constant editing.

image.alt: Creative work taking shape inside a minimal studio

sections.heading: Collect and Question
paragraphs: References come from typography, architecture, conversations and ordinary details. We keep only what supports the central idea.

sections.heading: Test in Context
paragraphs: Artwork is printed, worn and observed at real scale. A successful composition has to remain clear from across a room and interesting up close.

sections.heading: Make the Final Call
paragraphs: The last stage is subtraction. We remove competing details so the final garment feels confident rather than crowded.

blogArticles.pullQuote: The studio is less about inspiration than it is about better decisions.

blogArticles.title: Designing for Self-Expression
blogArticles.author: Percent Journal
blogArticles.excerpt: Why clothing should feel personal rather than repetitive.
blogArticles.introduction: Good clothing supports the person inside it. It creates room for expression without demanding that everyone look the same.

image.alt: Individual fashion styling in an editorial setting

sections.heading: Design as a Starting Point
paragraphs: We create a clear point of view, but never a complete instruction. The wearer decides what the piece becomes in daily life.

sections.heading: Silhouette and Confidence
paragraphs: Fit changes posture and movement. Standard and oversized forms offer different energies while preserving the same design language.

sections.heading: Make It Personal
paragraphs: The best styling choice is the one that feels recognisable to you, not the one most frequently repeated by others.

blogArticles.pullQuote: Clothing should frame identity, not replace it.

blogArticles.title: Less Ordinary.
blogArticles.author: Percent Journal
blogArticles.excerpt: The thinking behind the Percent identity.
blogArticles.introduction: Less Ordinary is not a request to be louder. It is an invitation to choose with more care and wear with more confidence.

image.alt: Minimal fashion campaign built around individual identity

sections.heading: A Clear Point of View
paragraphs: Percent exists between simplicity and expression. We use familiar forms, then introduce one decision that makes them distinct.

sections.heading: More You
paragraphs: The brand mark matters less than the person wearing it. Our role is to make pieces that support rather than overpower individual character.

sections.heading: Keep Moving
paragraphs: Every retired design makes space for a new direction. The identity remains consistent because the intention remains consistent.

blogArticles.pullQuote: Less ordinary does not mean more noise. It means more of you.

blogArticles.title: From Fabric to Final Piece
blogArticles.author: Percent Journal
blogArticles.excerpt: A closer look at material, print and production decisions.
blogArticles.introduction: The final piece is shaped by dozens of small choices that are rarely visible but always felt.

image.alt: Premium cotton garment prepared for final production

secondaryImage.alt: Finished apparel showing material and print detail

sections.heading: Begin With the Hand Feel
paragraphs: Weight, softness and recovery determine how a shirt lives beyond its first wear. The material must feel substantial without becoming rigid.

sections.heading: Print With Precision
paragraphs: Ink, pressure and placement are calibrated to suit the artwork and fabric. Consistency matters across every piece in the edition.

sections.heading: Inspect Every Detail
paragraphs: Each garment is checked before release so the experience feels considered from first touch to final wear.

blogArticles.pullQuote: Quality is the accumulation of decisions no one should have to notice.

blogArticles.title: Uniforms, Reconsidered
blogArticles.author: Percent Journal
blogArticles.excerpt: Building a personal wardrobe without becoming predictable.
blogArticles.introduction: A reliable wardrobe can still carry identity. Repetition becomes personal when proportion, texture and detail are chosen intentionally.

image.alt: A minimal everyday wardrobe styled with intention

sections.heading: Repeat the Foundation
paragraphs: Strong everyday pieces reduce noise and make room for personal details. Consistency can be a signature rather than a limitation.

sections.heading: Change the Proportion
paragraphs: Fit creates variation without requiring excess. A familiar palette can feel completely different through shape and layering.

sections.heading: Keep One Point of Tension
paragraphs: An unexpected graphic, texture or accessory keeps a uniform from becoming anonymous. One deliberate contrast is often enough.

blogArticles.pullQuote: A uniform becomes personal through the choices that break its pattern.
